newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. drug problem weighs on Hoechst.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drug problem weighs on Hoechst.

text.p: A proposal by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to withdraw approval for the allergy drug Seldane weighed on shares in Germany's Hoechst AG in pre-bourse dealings on Tuesday, dealers said.
The shares were down one mark at 69.30 marks at 0755 GMT, making them the biggest early decliners. The shares also showed the highest turnover in an otherwise quiet session.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index, which measures electronic dealings in the 30 DAX stocks, was estimated at 2,952.48, just below its close on Monday.

The FDA said on Monday that it intended to withdraw its approval for Seldane, or terfenadine, which is marketed by a U.S. unit of Hoechst, because of concerns over the safety of terfenadine-based drugs.
The FDA said it had recently approved Allegra, also marketed by Hoechst, which contains fexofenadine that has the same benefits as terfenadine but not the risks.
However Hoechst's Kansas City-based unit said it did not intend to withdraw Seldane from the market and would seek a hearing on the matter.
